title: running total
prompt: Write a Python function running_total(numbers) that takes a list of numbers and returns a new list in which each element is the sum of all elements of the input up to and including that position. For example, [1, 2, 3] gives [1, 3, 6]. An empty list gives an empty list.
requirements: Returns the cumulative sums in input order
Handles the empty list
Works for negative numbers and floats, not only positive integers
Returns a new list and does not mutate the input
reference_solution:
def running_total(numbers):
    out = []
    total = 0
    for x in numbers:
        total += x
        out.append(total)
    return out

title: clamp values
prompt: Write a Python function clamp_values(numbers, low, high) that returns a new list in which every number smaller than low is replaced by low, every number greater than high is replaced by high, and all other numbers are unchanged. Assume low <= high.
requirements: Values below low become low; values above high become high

Handles the empty list
reference_solution:
def clamp_values(numbers, low, high):
    return [min(max(x, low), high) for x in numbers]

title: top words
prompt: Write a Python function top_words(text, n) that returns the n most frequent words in the text as a list of (word, count) tuples, ordered by descending count and alphabetically for ties. Words are maximal runs of ASCII letters, compared case-insensitively and returned in lowercase. If there are fewer than n distinct words, return them all; if n is 0, return an empty list.
requirements: Words are maximal runs of ASCII letters, lowercased
Sorted by descending count, then alphabetically
Returns at most n (word, count) tuples
Handles n = 0, empty text, and n larger than the number of distinct words
tests: assert top_words('the cat and the dog', 2) == [('the', 2), ('and', 1)]
assert top_words('x x y y z', 2) == [('x', 2), ('y', 2)]
assert top_words('z z z y y x', 3) == [('z', 3), ('y', 2), ('x', 1)]
assert top_words('A a B b b', 2) == [('b', 3), ('a', 2)]
reference_solution:
import re
from collections import Counter

def top_words(text, n):
    words = re.findall(r'[a-zA-Z]+', text.lower())
    counts = Counter(words)
    ranked = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))
    return ranked[:n]

title: parameterized SQL builder
prompt: Write a Python function build_query(table, columns, filters) that builds a parameterized SQL SELECT statement. table is the table name, columns is a non-empty list of column names, and filters is a dictionary mapping column names to required values. Return a tuple (sql, params) where sql uses '?' placeholders for the filter values (never inline the values) and params is a tuple of the filter values in the same order as their placeholders. Filter conditions are joined with AND in the dictionary's order, each formatted as 'name = ?'. Columns are joined with ', '. Example: build_query('users', ['id', 'name'], {'age': 30}) returns ('SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE age = ?', (30,)). With an empty filters dictionary there is no WHERE clause. Table and column names may contain only letters, digits, and underscores, must not start with a digit, and must not be empty; otherwise raise a ValueError.
requirements: Filter values appear only as '?' placeholders, never inlined in the SQL
params tuple matches placeholder order (dictionary order)
Identifier allow-list validation for table, columns, and filter keys (ValueError otherwise)
No WHERE clause when filters is empty; exact 'SELECT cols FROM table [WHERE ...]' format
tests: assert build_query('users', ['id', 'name'], {'age': 30}) == ('SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE age = ?', (30,))
assert build_query('logs', ['msg'], {'level': 'error', 'host': 'web1'}) == ('SELECT msg FROM logs WHERE level = ? AND host = ?', ('error', 'web1'))
assert build_query('t', ['c'], {'b': 2, 'a': 1}) == ('SELECT c FROM t WHERE b = ? AND a = ?', (2, 1))
assert build_query('items', ['a', 'b', 'c'], {}) == ('SELECT a, b, c FROM items', ())
assert build_query('user_logs', ['_id'], {'user_id': 7}) == ('SELECT _id FROM user_logs WHERE user_id = ?', (7,))
assert build_query('users2', ['id'], {'ok': True}) == ('SELECT id FROM users2 WHERE ok = ?', (True,))

sql, params = build_query('users', ['id'], {'name': "O'Brien"})
assert "O'Brien" not in sql and params == ("O'Brien",)

sql, params = build_query('users', ['id'], {'name': 'x; DROP TABLE users'})
assert 'DROP' not in sql and sql == 'SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?' and params == ('x; DROP TABLE users',)
assert build_query('a', ['b'], {'c': None}) == ('SELECT b FROM a WHERE c = ?', (None,))
